title: Banqueting Standards for the Guaranteed Guest Count
content:
The kitchen of a Private Event & Banquet Services venue buys, rosters and sets a room against one number: the final guaranteed guest count.

## Standard 1 — the deadline

The final guaranteed guest count must be given by the guarantee deadline printed against the package, measured in whole hours before the start of the event on the event date.

## Standard 2 — where no guarantee is given

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: "Where no guarantee is given by the deadline, the working guest count standing on the booking becomes the guarantee, and the client is billed against it as though they had confirmed it."

## Standard 3 — setting above the guarantee

The kitchen sets and prepares above the guarantee by the overset percentage printed against the package, and those extra places are not charged unless they are used.

## Standard 4 — fewer guests than guaranteed

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: "Where fewer guests attend than were guaranteed, the event is billed on the guaranteed count at the shortfall percentage printed against the package, applied to the per-guest value of the contracted event."

## Standard 5 — more guests than guaranteed

Where more guests attend than were guaranteed, every guest served is billed, and guests beyond the overset are billed at the same per-guest value without surcharge.

## Standard 6 — moving the guarantee

A guarantee may be raised after the deadline where the kitchen can still buy the food, and it may never be lowered after the deadline.

## Standard 7 — attrition and security

The attrition allowance printed against the package absorbs a shortfall against a contracted room or cover block before the shortfall percentage is applied, and a package whose allowance is small absorbs proportionately less. Security staff are required once the guaranteed count passes the threshold printed against the package, and are charged at the security rate printed against the same package for the hours the event runs.

The percentages and hours these standards turn on are the figures of the package, and they remain the package's figures notwithstanding the two clauses above that are no longer in force.

## Illustration on a hypothetical overset of 5 per cent

A guarantee of 200 guests is set and prepared to 210 places. Where 205 guests attend, every guest served is billed; the five places that were set and not used are not charged.
